competency_fulfillment.rationale: All 17 samples are one-step subtraction with both numbers below 20, and I recomputed every one: seed 500 gives 'There are 17 drinks.' and '9 drinks are taken away.' with keyed answer 8, seed 502 gives 'Team A scored 14 in the music store and Team B scored 8' with answer 6, seed 46 gives 15 minus 10 with answer 5. No arithmetic error found. Every item is answerable from the text alone: the three cloze items (seeds 44, 501, 603) render the complete sentence with no ___ at all, so no blank falls on a quantity the answer depends on.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sentence names two delivery modes, orally or in pictures, and both appear. The oral or word-problem mode is everywhere, for example seed 602 'Team A scored 10 in the school canteen and Team B scored 1'. The picture mode appears in seeds 55 and 500, where a symbol row precedes 'There are 12 frogs.' and 'There are 17 drinks.'; I counted the rows and they hold exactly 12 and 17 symbols, matching the stated counts, so the picture does not contradict the text.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Problem structure is right for Grade 1 Quarter 3: one step, small numbers, familiar contexts. The defect is in the student-facing wording. Seed 43 reads 'A classmate has 1 story chapters', a plural noun after the numeral 1, which is wrong English in text a Grade 1 child reads or hears read aloud. Single-word nouns are handled correctly, as seed 604 shows with 'A classmate has 1 lightstick', so the miss is confined to multi-word object names. Math and answerability are unaffected, which is why this is a concern and not a failure.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Five formatters appear across 17 samples: mcq, cloze (seed 44), error_detect (seed 50, 'Jose says the answer is 8. Is Jose correct?'), read_mcq (seed 55), and true_false (seed 72). Three semantic framings appear as well: comparison 'How many more scrolls does Daniel have?' at seed 42, difference of scores 'What is the difference in their scores?' at seed 45, and take-away '1 frog is taken away.' at seed 55.

competency_alignment.rationale: Nothing in these samples reaches past subtraction of whole numbers under 20. No multiplication, no place-value naming, no money, no regrouping vocabulary. The true_false item at seed 72 states 'The answer is 6. True or False?', where 6 is the value being judged rather than an operand, and the operands there are 6 and 0. The error_detect item at seed 50 keeps the same shape.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The bound is both numbers less than 20 and it holds literally. The largest operand in the set is 17, at seed 500 'There are 17 drinks.'; nothing reaches 20. Values above the bound appear only as distractors and never as operands: 26 in the seed 500 option list and 24 in the seed 501 option list. One distribution note: 9 of the 17 samples use a subtrahend of 0 or 1, for example seed 606 'A classmate has 0 clip highlights' and seed 604 'A classmate has 1 lightstick', which makes over half the set nearly effortless, though genuine bridging work is present at seeds 500, 501 and 502.
